eyebrow: Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration · Chapter Fifteen
subtitle: Lesson 77 · PostgreSQL Performance Tuning

eyebrow: MVCC: old row versions don't just disappear
code:
UPDATE  -> writes a NEW row version,
           marks the old one no-longer-current
DELETE  -> marks the row no-longer-visible

Both leave a DEAD TUPLE:
  invisible to new transactions,
  still occupying disk space
caption: This is what lets readers and writers avoid blocking each other.

code:
VACUUM orders;
  -> marks dead tuple space reusable
     (does NOT shrink the file)

VACUUM FULL orders;
  -> rewrites the whole table
     returns space to the OS
     requires an exclusive lock
caption: Autovacuum runs the ordinary VACUUM automatically once a table crosses a threshold.

eyebrow: Table bloat: when vacuuming falls behind
code:
SELECT relname, n_dead_tup, n_live_tup
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC;

n_dead_tup climbing, n_live_tup flat
  -> autovacuum tuned too conservatively,
     or a long-running transaction blocking cleanup
caption: Bloat wastes disk space and slows down every scan, sequential or indexed.
